messages.subject: Generator with different timeout and resources distribution
parts:
Hello, 

I wrote a simple simmer code below but I have three types of projects. Each type of projects uses very different number of machine A and machine B as well as different distributions (mean) of timeout. 

For example, 

project 1 starts at time 10, using 10 machine A with timeout 15 on average; using 50 machine B with timeout  5 on average;
project 2 starts at time 20, using 100 machine A with timeout  50 on average; using 500 machine B with timeout  20 on average;
project 3 starts at time 30, using 1000 machine A with timeout  500 on average; using 5000 machine B with timeout  100 on average


The code below only works for projects with the same number of machine A and B (10 and 50) as well as similar timeout for machine A and B (mean 15 and 5). How can I implement the above example in simmer? Thanks!

env <- simmer("machines")
env

project <- trajectory("project path") %>%
  
  seize("machine A", 10) %>%
  timeout(function() rnorm(1, 15)) %>%
  release("machine A", 10) %>%
  
  seize("machine B", 50) %>%
  timeout(function() rnorm(1, 5)) %>%
  release("machine B", 50)

env %>%
  add_resource("machine A", 100) %>%
  add_resource("machine B", 100) %>%
  add_generator("project", project, function() rnorm(1, 10, 2))

Dear Iñaki,  

The purpose of this simulation is to try to maximize the usage of machine A and B. 

For the same example, 

There are 1000 machine A and 1000 machine B available. There are four types of projects, each type uses 100, 200, 500 and 400 machine A with different timeouts. 
Project 1 (type 1) uses 100 machine A; 
project 2 (type 2) uses 200 machine A; 
project 3 (type 3) uses 500 machine A; 
project 4 (type 4) uses 400 machine A, so project 4 will wait until project 1 finishes machine A step.

Project 5 can start even if project 1 is not finished, so all 1000 machine A can be utilized as many as possible each day. How do I decide which project a new arrival will follow? Each new arrival follows in one of the four types of projects. It is not completely random. I know in advance which new arrivals have which project type. How can I code this in branch? Also how can I code the above example so a later arrival can start earlier if it uses fewer machines? 

Thanks so much!

env

project <- trajectory("project path") %>%
branch(sample(1:4,size=1,replace=T), continue = c(T, T, T, T),   ### this means the new arrival is randomly assigned to one of the four project types but in reality it is not random

  seize("machine A", 100) %>%
  timeout(function() rnorm(1, 15)) %>%

  seize("machine B", 300) %>%

seize("machine B", 500) %>%
  timeout(function() rnorm(1, 20)) %>%
  release("machine B", 500))

env %>%
  add_resource("machine A", 1000) %>%

Dear Iñaki, 

Thanks for your suggestions, I added separate generators for each trajectory (each project type) and the arrival time for each generator. The problem is that I know each project type's arrival time but they are random so I can't use any distributions or functions for the arrival time for each project type. Is the code below correct? How should I specify the branch since the arrival time for each of the four project types are random? 

For the priority, fewer machines -> higher priority. That is true but if one project that needs more machines arrives and there are enough machines for this project, then this project will be initiated. But when there are not enough machines for this project, another project that arrives later but needs fewer machines will be initiated. How can we manage this kind of situation? 

Thanks so much!

There are 1000 machine A and 1000 machine B available. There are four types of projects, each type uses 100, 200, 500 and 400 machine A with different timeouts. 
Project 1 (type 1) uses 100 machine A; 
project 2 (type 2) uses 200 machine A; 
project 3 (type 3) uses 500 machine A; 
project 4 (type 4) uses 400 machine A, so project 4 will wait until project 1 finishes machine A step. 
project 5 (type 2) arrives slightly later than project 4 but it is the same type as project 2, which only uses 200 machine A, so project 5 can start earlier than project 4. Project 5 can start even if project 1 is not finished, so all 1000 machine A can be utilized as many as possible each day.

and there are enough machines, it means that there are no other

served. If a project with fewer machines arrives, then it will have

Dear Iñaki,

Thanks for your suggestions, I added separate generators for each trajectory (each project type) and the arrival time for each generator. The problem is that I know each project type's arrival time but they are random so I can't use any distributions or functions for the arrival time for each project type. Is the code below correct? How should I specify the branch since the arrival time for each of the four project types are random?

Do you mean that you have a vector of arrival times (probably
something measured in a real setup) and you know the type for each
arrival? Then use add_dataframe instead of add_generator. See
https://www.enchufa2.es/archives/simmer-3-8-0.html

If you split your data frame in several data frames by type, then you
can feed each project trajectory individually instead of using a
branch.

For the priority, fewer machines -> higher priority. That is true but if one project that needs more machines arrives and there are enough machines for this project, then this project will be initiated. But when there are not enough machines for this project, another project that arrives later but needs fewer machines will be initiated. How can we manage this kind of situation?

I don't see the problem. If a project that needs more machines arrives
and there are enough machines, it means that there are no other
projects with fewer machines waiting in the queue, so it will be
served. If a project with fewer machines arrives, then it will have
priority and it will be initiated.


Thanks so much!


There are 1000 machine A and 1000 machine B available. There are four types of projects, each type uses 100, 200, 500 and 400 machine A with different timeouts.
Project 1 (type 1) uses 100 machine A;
project 2 (type 2) uses 200 machine A;
project 3 (type 3) uses 500 machine A;
project 4 (type 4) uses 400 machine A, so project 4 will wait until project 1 finishes machine A step.
project 5 (type 2) arrives slightly later than project 4 but it is the same type as project 2, which only uses 200 machine A, so project 5 can start earlier than project 4. Project 5 can start even if project 1 is not finished, so all 1000 machine A can be utilized as many as possible each day.


env <- simmer("machines")
env

project <- trajectory("project path") %>%

 branch(??????, continue = c(T, T, T, T),   ### this means the new arrival is randomly assigned to one of the four project types but in reality it is not random

          seize("machine B", 500) %>%

          seize("machine B", 500) %>%
          timeout(function() rnorm(1, 20)) %>%

env %>%

 add_resource("machine B", 1000) %>%

### project type 1 arrives at time 5, 12, 20
 add_generator("project", project_type_1, at(5,12,20), priority=1) %>%

### project type 2's inter-arrival time is 8
 add_generator("project", project_type_2, function() rnorm(1, 8)) %>%

 add_generator("project", project_type_3, at(0,15)) %>%

On Tue, 29 Jan 2019 at 17:17, Zhou Fang <fangzh...@gmail.com> wrote:

Dear Iñaki,

The purpose of this simulation is to try to maximize the usage of machine A and B.

For the same example,

There are 1000 machine A and 1000 machine B available. There are four types of projects, each type uses 100, 200, 500 and 400 machine A with different timeouts.
Project 1 (type 1) uses 100 machine A;
project 2 (type 2) uses 200 machine A;
project 3 (type 3) uses 500 machine A;
project 4 (type 4) uses 400 machine A, so project 4 will wait until project 1 finishes machine A step.
project 5 (type 2) arrives slightly later than project 4 but it is the same type as project 2, which only uses 200 machine A, so project 5 can start earlier than project 4. Project 5 can start even if project 1 is not finished, so all 1000 machine A can be utilized as many as possible each day. How do I decide which project a new arrival will follow? Each new arrival follows in one of the four types of projects. It is not completely random. I know in advance which new arrivals have which project type. How can I code this in branch?

Well, if you know in advance, then encode it in a function. Which
parameters do you need for that? Use them in a function. If you can
define separate generators, it is much easier.

Also how can I code the above example so a later arrival can start earlier if it uses fewer machines?

This means that fewer machines -> higher priority. So you can define a
priority system based on this (see set_prioritization). Again, if you
can define separate generators, it is easier because each generator
has a static "priority" parameter, which is perfect for this.


Thanks so much!

env

Because that's not a function, but the result of a single run of a

branch(function() sample(1:4,size=1,replace=T), continue = c(T, T, T, T), ...
